description: Share the Tiiny device safely during a run: detect a Tiiny run (provider pi, a model id starting with tiiny/), take tiiny-router's cross-agent device lock and a hold file, load the run's models before the first agent starts, recover from not-loaded failures without spending a retry, release everything on every exit path, and warn when --effort or --concurrency cannot help on the device. Source: tasks/prd-tiiny-device.md. A run that is not a Tiiny run behaves exactly as it does today. Tests use a fake device HTTP server and a temp TIINY_HOME, never a real device, and assert observable results (exit code, lock and hold file contents, models the fake server was asked to load, ticket status, learnings outcome), never message wording.

userStories.title: Device client: list resident models and load a model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a small client that can tell which models are resident on the device and load one, so the run can start with its models in place.
acceptanceCriteria: residentModels() calls GET <baseUrl>/models with Authorization: Bearer <key> and returns the ids in data[].id
A network error or non-200 response from residentModels() is returned as an error value, not thrown
loadModel(id) first POSTs <host>/api/v1/models/<id>/start with the same bearer, where <host> is TIINY_HOST or http://tiinyhost.local
If the HTTP start fails, loadModel(id) falls back to running `script -q /dev/null <tiiny> load <id> -y`, where <tiiny> is TIINY_BIN or ~/.local/tiiny/bin/tiiny
After either path, loadModel polls residentModels() every 2 seconds until id is listed or 180 seconds pass (poll interval and deadline may be parameters so tests run fast)

userStories.title: Device lock compatible with tiiny-router
userStories.description: As a user running redeye and tiiny-router on one machine, I want them to use the same lock file, shape and flock, so they never generate on the device at the same time.
acceptanceCriteria: Lock path is TIINY_LOCK_FILE if set, else $TIINY_HOME/tiiny-lock.json, with TIINY_HOME defaulting to ~/.pi/agent/tiiny

A held lock is written as JSON {state:'held', owner, task, models, created, expires, pid} with created and expires in Unix seconds (floats allowed); a released lock is {state:'released', owner, task, released, pid}
acquire takes the lock when the file is missing, released, or held with expires in the past
acquire renews (extends expires) when the current holder has the same owner
acquire fails when another owner holds an unexpired lock, and the error names that owner, its task and the expiry time

Every read-modify-write of the lock file runs inside an exclusive flock on that file (the same primitive as Python fcntl.flock, e.g. via a short python3 helper or a native dependency); if the flock is busy, acquire reports that and does not write
release writes the released state (a write, not a delete) and succeeds only when redeye's owner matches the holder
redeye's owner string is redeye:<feature>:<pid> and the task is the feature name
Tests use a temp TIINY_HOME and assert lock file contents for: acquire on missing, acquire on expired, renew by same owner, refusal by another owner, release, release by a non-owner refused
npm run lint passes
npm test passes (after npm run build)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Reserve the device and load models before the first worktree
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Tiiny run to take the device and make sure its models are loaded before any agent starts.
acceptanceCriteria: For a Tiiny run without --no-device-lock, before the first worktree is created, redeye in order: acquires the lock with TTL --device-lock-ttl, writes the hold with the run's device model ids, loads each id that is not resident, then checks every id is resident
If another owner holds the lock, redeye exits non-zero before creating any worktree; the lock file is left unchanged
If any model is still not resident after loading, redeye clears the hold, releases the lock and exits non-zero
With --no-device-lock, redeye does not touch the lock or hold and does not ask the device to load anything

Integration tests use the fake device server and a temp TIINY_HOME and assert: models the fake server was asked to load, lock file state, hold file content, exit code, and that no worktree was created on refusal

npm test passes (after npm run build)

userStories.title: Renew the lock during the run and release on every exit path
userStories.description: As a user, I want redeye to keep the device while it runs and give it back however the run ends.
acceptanceCriteria: While a Tiiny run is in progress, redeye renews the lock every 5 minutes (a test-only env var may shorten the interval); a test shows expires moves forward during a run
The renewal timer does not keep the process alive after the run ends
After a run that finishes with all tickets done, the lock file is in the released state and the hold file is empty or missing
Same for a run with failed tickets (exit 1) and a run that ends in a runtime error (exit 2)
On SIGINT and SIGTERM, release and hold clear run in the existing handlers in src/index.ts before exit; exit codes stay 130 and 143
Release and hold clear do not throw when the lock was never taken, and their errors are logged, never change the exit code

userStories.title: Classify not-loaded failures
userStories.description: As a user, I want an attempt that failed because the model was not loaded to be reported as such, not as no-commits.
acceptanceCriteria: After a pi agent exits, redeye scans its --mode json stream for an assistant message_end with stopReason 'error' and an errorMessage containing 'is not loaded' or 'model_not_found'
This check runs before the no-commits check
'not-loaded' is added to LEARNING_OUTCOMES in src/learnings.ts; its entry names the model and is parsed back like the existing outcomes
Without recovery (e.g. --no-device-lock), a not-loaded attempt is a failed attempt that counts toward --retries
The fake pi agent (test/mock-agent-pi.js) can emit a not-loaded error stream and exit 0, driven by a FAKE_PI_* env var added to the tests' key lists
Tests assert the learnings outcome and ticket status, not wording

userStories.title: Reload and re-run after a not-loaded failure
userStories.description: As a user, I want an attempt that failed only because the model was evicted to be re-run after a reload, so it does not cost a retry or get the ticket skipped.
acceptanceCriteria: On a not-loaded failure in a Tiiny run holding the lock, redeye reloads the model with loadModel while still holding the lock, then re-runs the same attempt from a fresh worktree
The re-run does not count toward --retries, does not wait --retry-delay, and does not raise the effort level
Each attempt is recovered at most 2 times; after that it is an ordinary failed attempt
If the reload fails, the attempt is an ordinary failed attempt and its learnings entry says the model could not be reloaded
Each recovery appends a not-loaded learnings entry naming the model
With --no-device-lock, there is no reload (US-009 behavior)
Integration tests with the fake device and fake pi assert: models the fake server was asked to load, number of agent runs, ticket status, learnings outcomes
